How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

  C. MAYOR’S APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES –
  COUNCIL LIAISONS

  The Mayor is responsible for appointing members of the City Council to serve
  on various local and regional committees, as well as liaisons for City initiatives.
  In addition, it is necessary for the Council to take formal action to designate the
  new Mayor to serve as the Delegate to the Los Angeles County Sanitation
  District Board and Los Angeles County City Selection Committee. There is no
  fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-18 confirming
  the Mayor’s appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates
  and liaisons to outside agencies and Committees.

  D. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-05 TO HARDY AND HARPER,
  INCORPORATED FOR THE ANNUAL STREETS PROGRAM FISCAL YEAR
  2023-2024 IN THE AMOUNT OF $2,609,944.64 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  As part of the City’s ongoing effort to improve and preserve the quality of our
  roadways, the Public Works Department has developed the annual streets
  program for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. This street rehabilitation project will extend
  the service life by 10 to 20 years, restore the appearance of the pavement and
  inhibit further deterioration of approximately four road miles with an average
  Pavement Condition Index of below 20. Los Angeles County Public Works
  desires to join the City on this year’s Annual Streets Program to repave their
  owned portions of Broadway and Walnut Grove Avenue. In the event that the
  Los Angeles County Board does not approve the funding at the May 7, 2024
  board meeting, the City will not be obligated to pay for work not done on behalf
  of Los Angeles County and the contract price will be adjusted downward. Funds
  are available in the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 approved budget in the amount of
  $2,815,237.60, which includes a 10% construction contingency.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 2, 2024  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to Categorical Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – Existing Facilities.
  The project will improve the existing condition of local streets. No potential for
  significant impacts to the environment are anticipated in this project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve plans and specifications for the Annual Streets Program Fiscal Year
  2023-2024;
  2. Award the contract to Hardy and Harper, Incorporated;
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23-05;
  and
  4. Approve a purchase order in the amount of $2,815,237.60, which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

  E. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 24-01 TO VIDO SAMARZICH,
  INCORPORATED FOR THE SIDWALK AND PEDESTRIAN RAMP
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECT FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $123,880 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY [RESOLUTION NO. 24-15]

  The Public Works Department is responsible for the maintenance of all public
  sidewalks and installation of Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliant
  pedestrian ramps within the City. ADA pedestrian ramps provide a smooth and
  safe path of travel from the sidewalk to the street for people with disabilities.
  There is a substantial backlog of sidewalk maintenance needs and new ramp
  requests, and staff is seeking assistance from outside contractors. The cost to
  repair the sidewalks on Gerona Avenue is $47,630 and the cost to construct
  eight ADA curb ramps is $76,250 plus an additional 10% contingency amount
  of $12,388 for a total project budget of $136,268.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorically Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – Existing
  Facilities. The project will replace existing sidewalks and install ADA pedestrian
  ramps within the public right-of-way facilities. Irrespective of the exemption, no
  potential for significant impacts to the environment are anticipated from this
  project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-15 to appropriate additional $21,098 from the TDA
  Article 3 Fund to account 122-800-44-96-604;

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 2, 2024  4
   2. Approve plans and specifications for the Sidewalk & Pedestrian Ramp
  Improvement Project, Fiscal Year 2023-24;
  3. Award contract to Vido Samarzich, Incorporated;
  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 24-01;
  and
  5. Approve a purchase order in the amount of $136,268, which includes a 10%
  construction contingency.

  F. FIREWORK DISPLAY PERMIT – SAN GABRIEL COUNTRY CLUB

  Pyro Spectaculars, a California State Licensed Pyrotechnics Company, has
  applied for a permit on behalf of the San Gabriel Country Club, for a Fireworks
  Display on June 29, 2024, at 9:00 p.m. The display will last for approximately 30
  minutes. Pursuant to San Gabriel Municipal Code Title IX, Sections 96.21 – 96.23,
  City Council approval is required to issue a permit on approval and
  recommendation of the Fire Chief for pyrotechnic displays. A fee of $79 is due
  at the time of permit issuance per the Fiscal Year 23-24 Master Fee Schedule.
  No Fire Department overtime expense is anticipated for this event.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Fire Chief or Deputy Fire
  Marshal to issue a Fireworks Permit to Pyro Spectaculars, Incorporated
  contingent on meeting the conditions of the application.

  G. 2022 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY PROGRAM GRANT ACCEPTANCE
  [RESOLUTION NO. 24-09]

  The United States Department of Homeland Security provides grant funding to
  state and local governments through the State Homeland Security Program
  (SHSP) administered by the County of Los Angeles as subgrantee. The City of
  San Gabriel has been awarded grant funds from the 2022 State Homeland
  Security Program for both the San Gabriel Police and Fire Departments in the
  amount of $51,363 and $10,000 respectively. Acceptance of the grant funding
  and authorization to expend those funds on identified qualifying projects
  would enhance the capabilities of both public safety departments. Budget
  adjustments to Other Grants fund will be made to revenues and appropriations
  in the amount of $61,363. Funding for the purchases will be reimbursed
  through the State Homeland Security Program grant. Initial outlay would be

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 2, 2024  5
   $61,363, but would be fully reimbursed, with no matching funds. Consequently,
  there is no fiscal impact to the General Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-09 to approve
  the following:

  Police Department

  1. Budget amendment to increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and
  appropriation (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants Fund by $51,363; and increase
  estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special
  Projects Funds (account 124-751-57-99-380) by $51,363;

  Fire Department

  2. Budget amendment to increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and
  appropriation (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants Fund by $10,000; and increase
  estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special
  Projects Funds (account 124-761-57-99-380) by $10,000;

  3. Authorize both the Police Chief and Fire Chief to accept the State Homeland
  Security Program grant and purchase the items under the City’s purchasing
  policy; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute the subrecipient agreement between
  the City and the County of Los Angeles.

  H. GRANT-FUNDED PURCHASE OF RADIO EQUIPMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $30,114.99

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is seeking approval to spend $30,114.99 of
  previously-awarded State Homeland Security Grant funds on Motorola
  APX8500 radio equipment. In 2021, the Fire Department received a Homeland
  Security Grant Program award of $62,000 to fund the purchase of radio
  equipment. On May 2, 2023, the City Council accepted the grant award and
  appropriated funds by Resolution No. 23-21. $30,114.99 is a portion of the total
  amount previously awarded by the 2021 State Homeland Security Program
  (SHSP) grant cycle and requires no matching funds.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 2, 2024  6
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-20 authorizing State Homeland Security Grant
  Program-Funded Purchase of certain Motorola Radio Equipment in the
  Amount of $30,114.99; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to issue a purchase order to Motorola Solutions,
  Incorporated in an amount not to exceed $30,114.99 for the purchase of
  three APX8500 mobile radios and accessories detailed in the report in
  accordance with the City of San Gabriel purchasing policy and conditions of
  the 2021 State Homeland Security Program Grant award.

  I. APPROVAL OF A LETTER OF INTENT AGREEMENT WITH THE TAIWAN
  TOURISM ADMINISTRATION LOS ANGELES OFFICE FOR THE ACCEPTANCE
  OF A GIFT OF LANTERNS FOR THE SAN GABRIEL LUNAR LANTERN
  FESTIVAL

  The Taiwan Tourism Administration has generously offered to donate lanterns
  from the annual Lantern Festival in Taiwan (R.O.C.) to the City of San Gabriel, at
  no cost to the City. The proposed Letter of Intent Agreement memorialized the
  terms of the donation. There is no fiscal impact associated with the acceptance
  of lanterns from the Taiwan Tourism Administration. All shipping costs to
  receive the donation are being paid for by the Administration.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines, as it has no potential to
  significantly impact the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  It is recommended that the City Council approve the attached Letter of Intent
  Agreement and authorize the Mayor to execute the Agreement.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 2, 2024  7
   A. DISCUSSION AND DIRECTION ON AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA)
  RELOCATION GRANTS

  In 2023, the City launched a Small Business Assistance Grant Program utilizing
  the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds. The program had two components:
  General Assistance and Relocation Assistance. The General Assistance grants
  have been awarded to eligible small businesses. The Relocation Assistance
  grants have yet to be awarded given the recent direction of City Council to staff
  to further discuss the program parameters. This report provides a recap of the
  history of the program, applications received, and outlines the program’s
  guidelines. Per Council’s request, this item is being presented for further
  discussion of guidelines and requirements by the Council. The remaining
  authorized funding for the relocation grants in the amount of $95,000 has been
  carried forward and is included in the Fiscal Year 2023-24 general fund budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff is seeking direction from the Council on how to implement the Relocation
  Assistance Program.

  B. DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL: 2023 RECAP AND SELECTING EVENT
  PARTNER

  The Dumpling and Beer Festival was introduced in 2015 to showcase the
  culinary aspect of the City and attract tourism to the Mission District. Over the
  years, the festival has grown into a community event that celebrates diversity
  and culture through popular food and drink. Each year, the event attracts
  around 5,000 – 7,000 visitors, and this number continues to grow. This is a
  ‘receive and file’ report that outlines staff’s extensive planning efforts that
  contribute to the festival’s yearly success. The timing of the report also presents
  an opportunity for the City to possibly explore partnering with other non-profit
  organizations for the event. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 2, 2024  8
   Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report and discuss

  the matter of partnerships, specifically as it relates to selecting the non-profit
  that the City works with for the Festival.
